# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and inspect only the expected
vault paths needed by the task. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
For unavailable, rejected or uncertain requests, follow the direct
[app diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#failure-refusal-and-uncertain-mutation).
A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome: inspect the exact target before
retrying or switching channels. Never claim a filesystem fallback executed an
app-only action. No fallback implicitly authorizes a write.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

For Windows redirector and empty-output diagnosis, read
[app access](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#windows-invocation) only
when needed. These reporting examples are read-only: no operation or rebuild is
needed to answer a question.

# Keeping knowledge findable and trustworthy

Use this contract when creating concepts, linking topics, discovering sources or reviewing answers. The schema stays small; explanatory prose supplies the nuance.

## Concept identity

Before creating a concept, search its intended title, common alternative wording, and the nearest existing concepts. Choose explicitly: extend the canonical page, add an equivalent alias, or create a distinct concept with a scope boundary. Use the direct [identity check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#identity-and-relationship-checks) when ambiguity is suspected. Never merge based on embedding similarity alone.

Use `aliases: ["equivalent phrase"]` and a one-sentence `scope:` on concept pages. Aliases name the same concept; broader, narrower and complementary concepts remain separate pages. Use full-path wikilinks for ambiguous names. A source page and a concept may legitimately share a basename; a warning is a review queue, not permission to rename everything.

Two rules decide a bare name before it counts as ambiguous. A file whose own name equals the link outranks files that only share that name as a `title:` or alias (a site that serves a case's syllabus and opinion under one title gives two clippings one title; the clipping named for the link is the one Obsidian opens). And in navigation a project's generated hub MOC (`moc/<project>.md`) yields to a page of the same name, so a bare `[[<project>]]` reaches the entity page; the MOC is still reached by `[[moc/<project>]]`. Two files with the same name stay ambiguous. After a refresh scoped to one project, the result's `staleCatalogs` names other projects' generated catalogs whose bare link your new pages made ambiguous; refresh each named project.

## Relationships and citations

Keep citations in `sources:` and in the prose they support. Citation targets point to `wiki/sources/` or `raw/`, using full paths when needed. A source page must identify its own raw clipping. Reachable evidence establishes a citation route, not that a claim is true or entailed by it.

Put navigation in `## Relationships` or `Related:`. Use a small role vocabulary: **broader**, **narrower**, **prerequisite**, **complements**, **alternative**, **contrasts**, **applies-to**. Each link needs a sentence explaining the relationship and its limits. For example: `Complements [[wiki/concepts/Intention-Action Gap.md|Intention–Action Gap]]: this intervention addresses a gap between intending and acting under the conditions described above.` Do not turn similar wording into a causal claim. Clearly label cross-source interpretations as synthesis; retain their supporting citations outside the navigation section.

Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/relationships.mjs" --limit=10 --json` to generate candidates. Shared sources and semantic neighbors are reasons to inspect, never proof of a relationship. Review both pages and their evidence; accept only links with a useful explanation. Reuse existing user authorization for the requested relink scope. Do not grow links merely to improve a graph score.

## Task maps and discovery

Curated `moc/` maps answer a recurring task: where to start, prerequisites, competing approaches, complementary domains, and unresolved questions. Keep generated project catalogs as a section or separate linked page. Search indexes both wiki pages and MOCs. Maintain a few useful maps instead of a universal taxonomy.

Discovery starts with an unanswered question and bounded search of the existing wiki/MOCs. Each candidate source must state what evidence it adds and which existing or proposed concept/synthesis it changes. Deduplicate source URLs as before. Read the manual Start here section of `index.md` only if needed; never load its generated catalog as the default coverage summary. Promote high-use stubs and missing bridges when their current evidence is sufficient; do not pad stubs or enforce a source:synthesis ratio.

## Verification obligations

Each ingest or substantive edit verifies identity and citation paths, updates the
affected task map, and completes the operation. `reviewed` means factual claims
were checked; `updated` means edited; index freshness is a file-version match.
None substitutes for another. Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.
Use [checks and cadence](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#verification-cadence)
for diagnostic procedures and bounded maintenance evaluation.

# Evidence and editorial policy

## Page schema and dates

Wiki frontmatter declares `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored),
`created`, `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources` and
honest `ai-generated` authorship. Follow the vault's schema; missing `reviewed`
means unverified, never substitute `updated`. Keep three dates distinct:
`updated` means edited, `reviewed` means claims checked against evidence or current
project behavior, and index freshness means indexed content matches the files.
Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.

Use exact citation paths and `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not
relationship edges. Write unwrapped logical lines and never split a wikilink over
a line break. Use [identity and relationships](efficacy.md) for concept reuse and
explained links. Original documentation follows
[authoring](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md).

## Non-negotiable guardrails
1. **`raw/` bodies are immutable.** Read raw sources; never edit their content —
   it is the evidence every wiki page cites. Frontmatter is pipeline state and
   may be updated by wiki-master tooling only.
   Only clipping tools create raw evidence; never move it to record ingestion
   state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
2. **Provenance on every claim.** Each wiki page you write carries `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
   linking back to the `raw/` notes it derives from, plus `ai-generated: true`.
   **Exception: `wiki/authored/`** — original content with no `raw/` counterpart
   (advisory documentation, policy, house style) declares this explicitly via
   `sources: []`, never by omission. `ai-generated` still records actual
   authorship (`true` if you drafted it, `false` if the human did) — the
   disclosure is about provenance, not about who wrote the words.
3. **Cite when you answer.** Query answers reference the pages/sources they rest on.
4. **Flag, don't invent.** If sources contradict or are silent, say so — never
   paper over a gap with plausible text.
5. **Clippings win.** Briefs, discovery summaries, corrections files, and your
   own memory of a source are *claims, not authority*: verify every quote,
   figure, and attribution against the clipping in `raw/` before it lands on a
   page, and when they disagree the clipping prevails — including when the
   instruction is the user's. Every layer between the source and the page is a
   lossy compressor whose errors read exactly like facts; authority flows
   outward from the one artifact that cannot drift.
   Scope edges, which matter as much as the rule:
   - It guarantees **fidelity, not truth** — a faithful clipping of a wrong page
     is still wrong; quality tiers and cross-clipping corroboration handle
     credibility.
   - A **degraded capture** (bad OCR, partial extraction) wins as evidence of
     what the vault *holds*, not of what the author typed — don't trust it at
     character level.
   - A clipping's **silence proves "not supported here," never "false"** —
     record unsourced claims as unsourced (visibly, on the page) rather than
     asserting or deleting them. The vault cannot cite what it does not hold.

## Reddit and Medium

Reddit posts and comments, and articles on medium.com or its subdomains, are
eligible sources. Keep their material in separate labeled sections in every
derived page and query answer: `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` for Reddit
and `## Medium articles` for Medium. Put platform-derived claims, quotes,
reported experiences and any inference that relies on them in the corresponding
section; do not blend the two platforms together or with higher-quality evidence.
This applies to source summaries, concepts, entities and syntheses, including
material reused through another wiki page. Even a summary of a single platform
source needs its heading. Raw clippings retain the captured content without rewriting.

Attribute statements to their authors and cite the captured evidence. For Reddit,
do not turn a few comments into consensus, prevalence or established facts.
Disclose missing comments or reply context when the capture is incomplete;
do not claim a full thread was captured without verifying it. Upvotes do not
establish credibility.

Keep Reddit and Medium citations and dependent conclusions out of the main factual
sections, opening summary and recommendations. A fact independently supported
by higher-quality evidence may appear there with those independent citations;
any platform comparison stays in its labeled section. Retain all provenance in
`sources:` frontmatter. Assess individual sources using the existing credibility
rubric; allowing capture does not automatically upgrade their credibility.
Official platform documentation and policy pages outside discussion threads or
Medium articles do not require these labels.

## Style: viewpoints whole, conclusions after, breadcrumbs always
Narrative is licensed; dismissal is not. Three house rules govern every page:

1. **Opposing viewpoints appear in their entirety** — in their own strongest
   terms, attributed to their holders — before any conclusion engages them.
   A viewpoint the page ends up arguing against gets the same care as one it
   endorses; weight follows the evidence the vault holds, and no viewpoint is
   waved off by tone (loaded verbs, scare quotes, "supposedly"). When sources
   conflict, keep the claims separate and attributed — never resolve them into
   one synthesized voice that erases the disagreement.
2. **Viewpoints first, conclusions after — and conclusions declare themselves.**
   Every analytic sentence is one of: *inherited* (a source says it — cite it),
   *extended* (built on a source — cite it, mark what's added), or *original*
   (the wiki's own inference — say so explicitly, never state it in the
   page's neutral voice). Joining source A to source B to imply C is an
   *original* claim even when A and B are both cited.
3. **The breadcrumb trail is non-negotiable.** Every viewpoint and every
   conclusion must be walkable back to `raw/`: `sources:` frontmatter, inline
   `[[wikilinks]]` to the source pages, and quotes verified per guardrail #5.
   A conclusion whose trail dead-ends is a defect, however good it reads.

Per-type licenses (neutrality is a property of a page type, not of the vault):
- `raw/` — fidelity only; the evidence layer (guardrail #1, #5).
- `wiki/entities/` — **describe and only describe.** Convert opinions to
  attributed facts about who holds them; convert evaluations to the measurable
  facts beneath them. When tempted to interpret, link to a concept or
  synthesis instead.
- `wiki/concepts/` — claims with grounding. Assertive titles are allowed; the
  title's pressure is the point, and the body must support the claim under
  rules 1–3.
- `wiki/syntheses/` — the licensed narrative layer: weigh, judge, conclude —
  bounded by rules 1–3, and labeled as the wiki's synthesis.
- `wiki/authored/` — the vault's own first-party voice: advisory documentation,
  policy, house style, or other original work with no `raw/` evidence behind it
  by design. Same full narrative license as syntheses; state recommendations
  directly. Rule 3 (breadcrumb to `raw/`) does not apply — there is deliberately
  nothing to trail, declared via `sources: []` rather than left silent.

Clippings carry `quality: high|medium|low`, an AI credibility rating. Treat low-quality sources with extra skepticism during ingestion; lint may flag claims supported only by low-quality provenance. Capture fidelity and source credibility are separate judgments.

`citation-status: quarantined` is an explicit do-not-cite restriction, independent of credibility and character fidelity. Do not use that capture as supporting evidence or repeat dependent claims without independent support. Citing pages may carry `citation-status: restricted` and a warning identifying the affected evidence. A different state, `citation-status: retired`, marks a note that is a lead and must not be cited as support: `health` does not ask it for evidence and reports any page that cites it (`cites-retired-page`). Do not use `retired` for a page that merely leans on a quarantined clipping; that is `restricted`, and it stays under the evidence check. Preserve the restriction when reusing summaries; removing an item from triage is not permission to cite it. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md).

HTML clips may also carry `fidelity: partial` and `fidelity-checks: <count>`. The clipper compares recognized source headings, callouts, availability notices, API introductions and feature-list items with extracted text, plus whole normalized endpoint summaries and parameter rows, and literal supplied code examples in recognized REST layouts. Missing probes queue fidelity triage. `fidelity-ignored: <count>` records headings set aside as site chrome (a feedback widget, a sidebar); they open no triage, and their labels are printed when the clip is made. Inspect the triage issues before quoting affected material. Zero warnings is not proof of completeness: unrecognized structures, unselected UI tabs and content absent from supplied HTML are outside this check. See [HTML clipping fidelity](../../../docs/clipping-fidelity.md).

A URL can have more than one capture. A recapture (`clip.mjs <url> --recapture`) is a second, dated clipping of the same page, written beside the first: its name and `title` end ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, its `created` is the day it was made, and `recapture-of` names the newest capture it follows, as a vault path. The older clipping is never edited, so both are evidence of what the page said on their own dates, each with its own `source-hash`; cite the capture whose text you quote. The ingest backlog treats two captures with different text as two sources. `extraction: manual` marks a page a person saved from a signed-in browser and supplied with `clip.mjs <url> --from-file <path>`: `source` is the page's real address, nothing was fetched, `supplied-sha256` is the hash of the supplied bytes (the file's name is not recorded) and `source-hash` that of the stored text. Like `ocr` and `rendered`, it names how the text was obtained and is not a defect. `apply-reclips` refuses such a clipping, because a fetched page would replace the supplied text; refresh it with `clip.mjs <url> --from-file <path> --recapture`. The clipper still refuses a supplied login, consent or age-gate page and a supplied page under 100 words. See [recapture, saved pages and the decline and known-URL commands](../../../docs/clipping-fidelity.md#recapture-saved-pages-and-the-decline-and-known-url-commands-0870).

# Correct factual claims and record reviewed findings

Read [access](access.md), [evidence](evidence.md), [identity](efficacy.md) and
[operation completion](operations.md). This procedure owns authorized corrections
and persisted dispositions. A report-only request uses [setup lint reporting](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#content-lint-report) and writes nothing.

1. Establish relevant findings through the direct [health check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog),
   [bounded maintenance evaluation](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#bounded-maintenance-evaluation)
   and [content lint](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#content-lint-report).
   Stop for an empty wiki; a clean graph still needs bounded claim review during
   substantive maintenance. Report the actual sample and failed/skipped coverage.
2. Read flagged pages and exact supporting clippings. Check the citation trail
   before correcting a quote: an ambiguous or misrouted citation can produce the
   apparent mismatch. Inspect contradictions, superseded claims, unwritten
   concepts and missing connections. Similarity is never truth verification.
3. Decide each finding from evidence. Restore omitted clauses or add an honest
   ellipsis for real gaps; correct actual drift against the clipping. Own wording,
   mention/title quotes and retracted claims may be conventions to ignore. Mark
   claims unsourced when support is absent; never invent evidence or edit raw
   text to agree with the summary. Route structural repairs to [repair](repair.md)
   within the authorized scope. Propose unresolved changes without applying them.
4. Before the first authorized edit or persisted disposition, open or reuse a
   **lint** operation and record exact owned paths. Set `updated` on edited pages;
   set `reviewed` only for claims actually checked against evidence or project
   behavior. Mechanical links, aliases and formatting preserve factual dates.
   For original authored documentation, use [project authoring](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md).
5. Persist reviewed dispositions when requested, so the same finding is not
   repeatedly presented as new. Obtain IDs through the linked lint procedure,
   then run:

   ```sh
   node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lint-disposition.mjs" record --ids=<id>,<id> --disposition=own-wording --reviewer=<name> --page=<path>
   ```

   Select the actual verdict: `own-wording`, `mention`, `title`, `markup` or
   `accepted`; use `fixed` only for a quote actually corrected. The supported
   scope choices are `--page=<path>`, `--paths-file=<ledger>` or `--whole-vault`;
   select only the authorized scope. Add `lint-dispositions.jsonl` to the operation
   ledger. A changed quote or replaced clipping is a new finding and needs a new
   reading; a finding still present after `fixed` is listed again.
6. Recheck the affected findings and [validate owned paths](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Refresh affected owned catalogs and complete one lint log, scoped commit,
   sync and remote verification through [operations](operations.md). If no edit
   or disposition was applied, return the report with no operation/log/commit.

**Done:** applied corrections are supported and verified, reviewed dispositions
match actual inspection, untouched raw evidence and factual dates are preserved,
and the owned operation is published or its hold/local-only/blocker is explicit.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/mainte.content:
# Maintenance contracts and content repairs

Use [checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md) for read-only health, metrics,
freshness and lint reporting. Apply repairs only within authorized content scope,
with [operations](operations.md), [evidence](evidence.md) and direct
[scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).

## "Has this been ingested?" — a content-hash join, not a guess
A raw clipping is **ingested iff its `source-hash` is recorded in some
`wiki/sources/` page's `source-hashes`**. Hash equality is the contract — immune to
the `-<hash7>` filename suffix and the citation-format drift that made
link-resolution manufacture phantom backlog. Only Markdown clippings are ingestable units; binary originals are not summary
targets. Use the direct [backlog check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog)
to obtain counts. Never derive eligibility from filename, title, a fuzzy citation
match or filesystem movement.

**Migrating a vault (agents, any machine).** A vault written before this scheme has
source pages without `source-hashes`; a transitional fallback keeps them credited by
link resolution so nothing regresses, but `backfillPending > 0` means the migration
has not run here. Repair it from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backfill-source-hashes.mjs"`
(dry-run) then `--apply`. It is idempotent and guesses nothing — ambiguous/unresolved
citations are logged for review. If the vault is git-synced, running it once and
committing repairs every machine.

**Repairing title-shaped citations (`provenanceGaps > 0`).** A separate, older drift:
ingest wrote `sources: ["[[<the source's title>]]"]`, but the clipper had already
slugified that title into the filename (`/`, `:`, `#` → `-`, 120-char cap). Any title
carrying one of those characters or running long cites a file that does not exist —
the page is a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, though the ingest
was correct. Repair from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"`
(dry-run) then `--apply`. It joins on `source-hash`, never on the title (the title is
what drifted), and reports anything it cannot pin to exactly one clipping instead of
guessing. Always cite a clipping by its **path**, `[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]`.

**Repairing hard-wrapped wikilinks (`health.mjs` defects marked "hard-wrapped
wikilink").** Hand- or LLM-authored prose that gets word-wrapped at some column width
can break a `[[Target]]` straddling the wrap point into `[[Target\ncontinued]]` —
Obsidian wikilinks cannot span a line break, so this can never resolve and is always a
defect, never a healthy deferred forward-link (`classifyBrokenLinks` never lets a
wrapped target hide there, whether or not a suggestion resolves). **Prevention that
actually holds**: write vault content as unwrapped logical lines — never hard-wrap a
paragraph, and never let one contain a `[[wikilink]]` split across a line break — the
same discipline `clip-docx`'s `--wrap=none` already enforces mechanically on the docx
path. A written reminder alone is not the safeguard: maintainer relink's own `op-commit`
step reports any wrapped link introduced by the files it just committed, and
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` always scores one as a defect, so either catches a recurrence
even if the writing habit doesn't. Repair existing ones from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-wrapped-links.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`. The fix is a lossless
whitespace-collapse (undoing the wrap, never guessing content); the one shape it cannot
safely resolve alone — a hyphen glued to the word right before the break, e.g.
`[[Diagno-\nstics]]`, indistinguishable by character shape from a title that
legitimately ends a line in a trailing hyphen (`[[Wizards-\n  Definition...]]`, a real
title) — is checked against the real page index (not edit-distance guessing) and only
fixed when exactly one reading resolves; left untouched and reported otherwise. See
`scripts/lib/dewrap-links.mjs`.

**Repairing invalid `sources:`/`source-hashes:` ordering.** A now-fixed bug in
`insertSourceHashes` could insert `source-hashes:` between a block-list `sources:`
key and its own `- [[...]]` item instead of after it — invalid YAML that a real
parser rejects outright, so Obsidian reports "No frontmatter found" on the page
(every property, not just `sources`) even though wiki-master's own regex-based
scripts tolerate it and never flagged it as a defect. Repair from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-sources-order.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`. Pure string
surgery — it recognizes and reorders only that exact shape and is a no-op on
anything else — idempotent and safe to re-run.

**Repairing ambiguous bare links.** A bare `[[architecture]]` is an `ambiguous-link` defect when two pages
share the name. From the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-ambiguous-links.mjs"` (dry
run, with the plan and the report) then `--apply`; `--project=<slug>` bounds it. On its own it applies one rule:
the page lives in a project's folder (`wiki/authored/<project>/`) and exactly one candidate does too, so the
link is rewritten to that path with the displayed text kept (`[[wiki/authored/<project>/architecture.md|architecture]]`;
`\|` inside a table row; an existing alias or `#heading` kept; a `sources:` entry takes the full path with no
alias). Links in code, comments and a generated catalog fence stay. Every other class is reported with its
reason, not guessed: a page outside every project folder (`shared-page`), several candidates or none in the
page's project (`needs-reading`), a title shared by two clippings (`title-citation`, repaired by retitling the
clippings, not from the citing page), an occurrence only inside a generated catalog (`catalog-line`, repaired by
regenerating it). A reviewed `--mapping=<file>` of `{ "target", "path", "page"? }` settles the ones that need a
reading, and only with a path that is a candidate. A page an application reads by title, where a path in a
citation would break it, is left alone with `--exclude=<path-prefix>` (repeatable). It sets `updated` to the run
date, leaves `reviewed`, and checks line by line that only wikilinks changed.

**Renaming clippings that Obsidian hides or a wikilink cannot carry.** Obsidian does
not index a dot-prefixed file, and `graph.mjs` skips the same names, so a clipping
filed as `.github-workflows-build.yml.md` is invisible: every citation of it is an
`unresolved-citation`, and an uncited one never reaches the ingest backlog. A backtick
in a filename is the same trap in another form (a backtick pair inside a wikilink reads
as a code span). The clippers now write `dot-github-workflows-build.yml.md` and drop
backticks (`scripts/lib/clip-names.mjs`); a re-clip of `clip-gh` adopts a file written
under its old name instead of copying it or, in digest mode, pruning it. Rename the
existing ones from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/rename-unsafe-clippings.mjs"` (dry-run), then
`--apply --paths-out <ledger.json>` inside an operation and close with
`op-commit --paths-file <ledger.json>`; the ledger lists the old names, the new names and
the pages rewritten. It renames only `.md` files under `raw/` (a state file such as
`raw/book-nom/.booknom-state.json` is hidden on purpose), leaves clipping content and
therefore `source-hash` alone, repoints full-path wikilinks in every page except `raw/`,
`log/` and `_templates/` (a link in a code block is an example and stays), reports other
mentions of an old path without rewriting them, and refuses a rename whose target exists.
Pages are rewritten before files are renamed, so an interrupted run is finished by running
it again.

**Renaming clippings whose names double the extension.** Before 0.58.0 a clipping of
`README.md` was filed `README.md.md`, and a title-less raw document `SKILL.md.md`; new clippings
no longer end `.md.md`. Rename the existing ones from the plugin root with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/rename-doubled-extension-clippings.mjs" --list-out <review.tsv>`
(dry run, writes nothing to the vault), review the listing, then `--apply --paths-out <ledger.json>`
inside an operation and close with `op-commit --paths-file <ledger.json>`. A `clip-gh` file
under `raw/clippings/gh/<owner>/<repo>/` loses its second `.md`; a top-level clipping with an empty
title is renamed from its source URL, nearest folder first, as new clips are. The contract is
the one above (bytes and `source-hash` untouched, full-path wikilinks only, `raw/` and `log/`
never rewritten, a rename onto an existing name refused), plus three more. A link to the
extension-stripped path is repointed only when no existing file has exactly that path (a vault
may hold both `Build.md` and `build.md.md`; a link to `Build.md` means the real file). The apply
refuses to start when any file it would change has uncommitted changes in the vault's git, because
another writer may be editing it, and changes nothing. `--flag=<prefix>` lists the pages under a prefix
for review and `--exclude=<prefix>` reports them without rewriting (both repeatable): use them for pages
whose citations an app reads by title. A bare-name link such as `[[README.md]]` is not rewritten.

**Backfilling `project:`/`kind:` onto pre-existing `wiki/authored/` pages.** A vault
whose authored pages predate this convention has none of it set. Repair from the
plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backfill-authored-metadata.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`
— deterministic, filename- and content-shape-driven classification (never a guess:
a field it cannot resolve confidently is left unset rather than labeled wrong), and
idempotent, so it is safe to re-run as new authored pages arrive without metadata
of their own yet.

**Never move files to record ingestion state.** `raw/` immutability is the
load-bearing invariant. The hash key lives *in* the markdown — each page's
`source-hashes`, co-located with the summary that owns it — a single source of truth
that merges cleanly across machines. Derive the backlog at read time from that key,
like `index.md`; never copy ingestion state into the filesystem layout, where it can
drift and where two concurrent sessions race on the move.

## Known limits of the pattern
Stated so they are not rediscovered as surprises. The pattern this vault
implements bounds itself in ways worth tracking:
- **Index-only navigation is untested past the scale the source reports.** The
  source pattern says it "works surprisingly well at moderate scale (~100 sources,
  ~hundreds of pages)" — a claim about where it works, **not a ceiling**. It names
  no threshold and no failure mode. Separately, under an *Optional* heading, it
  says "as the wiki grows you want proper search" and suggests `qmd`, attaching no
  number; the two passages are not joined in the source, so do not present ~100 as
  the trigger for adopting search tooling. What is fair to say: a vault far past
  that figure is outside the range the source reports, entry may have shifted from
  reading `index.md` to `obsidian search` without anyone noticing, and **nobody has
  measured whether that costs anything**. Say that, and say it is untested — do not
  upgrade it into a bound the source never stated.
- **Cheap maintenance is not correct maintenance.** The pattern's justification is
  that upkeep cost approaches zero, which addresses effort, not accuracy. It
  specifies no verification tier — that is what content lint, quote-lint, and the
  clipping-wins guardrail exist to supply.
- **Frictionless collection is not free.** Automated discovery plus automated
  ingest removes the cost that used to limit what got kept. Volume is not
  progress; prefer fewer, better-corroborated sources over a larger pile.

## Verification obligation

Validate actual repairs and inspect changed or high-use claims during substantive
maintenance. Use the direct [bounded checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#bounded-maintenance-evaluation)
for reporting procedures and coverage. A clean graph does not establish factual
correctness; do not change factual review dates for mechanical repairs.

Read directly for this operation: [access](access.md).
Select the calling workflow before mutations; CLI syntax alone does not authorize writes.

# Driving the Obsidian CLI

The vault is targeted by name: `obsidian vault=<name> <command> ...`. wiki-master
resolves `<name>` from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT_NAME` or the vault folder's basename, and
its **filesystem path** from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT`, defaulting to `~/.wiki-master-vault`
(this convention lives in `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` — the bundled scripts use it, so
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` and friends need no path argument). Start there rather than
searching the disk for the vault.
`file=` resolves by name (like wikilinks); `path=` is an exact vault-relative path.
Invoke commands through `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. Never bypass it with native CLI calls or run
parallel native commands. The shared lock has a bounded wait; busy means not sent.
Oversized or physically multiline requests are rejected before launch. Ordinary
Markdown bodies go through filesystem editing, even when the CLI works. Do not
chunk a rejected note into repeated CLI writes. Inspect the exact target first if
an earlier write's outcome is uncertain. See the directly linked access contract.
The guarded `vault info=path` command can confirm the root
when the app responds; the known configured/default root supports filesystem access
without that probe.

## Access failures and empty results

Use the direct [app-access diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md) for Windows invocation, lazy canary checks, failure/refusal and uncertain mutations. Do not probe before every action; no app is required for independent filesystem work. Before retrying any timed-out mutation, inspect the actual target.

## Syntax and the live contract
- **Parameters take `=`; flags are bare.** `create name="My Note" content="Hello"`
  vs `create name=Note open overwrite`. `\n` / `\t` for multiline content.
- **`vault=<name>` must be the first parameter**, before the command.
- **`format=` is a parameter, not a flag**, and its default varies per command —
  `search` defaults to `text`, `backlinks`/`tags`/`properties` to `tsv`,
  `base:query` to `json`. Never assume JSON; ask for it.
- **`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" help` outranks the docs.** Obsidian's own skill says it "is always
  up to date" — so when the published reference and the binary disagree, the
  binary wins. Check `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" help <command>` before concluding a flag is gone.
- Prior art worth comparing against: kepano (Obsidian's CEO) publishes a
  first-party `obsidian-cli` Agent Skill. Where it and this skill agree — `total`
  for counts, `file=` vs `path=`, vault-first ordering — the agreement is
  independent corroboration, not inheritance.

## Read / search
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" read path=wiki/concepts/alpha.md`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="tag:clippings neural" path=wiki limit=10 format=json`
- Scope to `path=wiki` by default — `raw/` holds immutable source dumps (one
  clipping can contain a long document) and belongs in results only when asked.
- Probe cost before fetching: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="..." total` (a count only).
- **Never default to `search:context`** — it returns every matching line from
  every file, and
  `limit=` bounds files, not lines, so it cannot save you. Escalate to
  `search:context` only with both `path=` and a narrow query.

## Links & graph
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" backlinks file=alpha counts` — who links here
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" links file=alpha` — outgoing links
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" unresolved verbose format=json` — broken links WITH source files.
  The bare form returns targets only; `verbose` is the difference between a
  defect you can act on and a string you can't attribute. Several subcommands
  have lossy defaults with a `verbose` escape — prefer `format=json verbose`.
- For content health use the direct [filesystem checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog), not app `orphans`/`deadends` as repair metrics.

## Typed properties (frontmatter)
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" property:set name=reviewed value=2026-07-15 type=date path=wiki/concepts/alpha.md`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" property:read name=reviewed path=...`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" properties path=...` — list a note's properties

## Create / edit / move
- Create, replace or append ordinary Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits
  under the known root, using the shared operation lifecycle. Preserve current
  content and raw evidence. Do not send substantial text through the CLI.
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" move file=foo to=wiki/entities`

## Tags, tasks, templates, bases
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" tags counts` · `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" tag name=neural verbose`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" base:query file=stale.base view=all format=json`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" template:insert name=source-note`

## Escape hatches
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" command id=<id>` — run any Obsidian command (`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" commands` to list)
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" eval code="<js>"` — arbitrary JS in app context (last resort).
  **This is remote code execution against the vault**, and it sits in the same
  namespace as the read-only subcommands: a blanket `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" *` permission grant
  covers it. It belongs in its own permission decision, not folded in with
  `search` and `read`. The same applies to `dev:cdp` and `dev:debug`.

If a command fails, report its diagnostic and use
[app failure recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/app-access.md#failure-refusal-and-uncertain-mutation).
Never claim a filesystem fallback performed an app-only action. For content
mutations, retain [operation completion](operations.md) and direct
[scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md); UI-only actions do
not manufacture content operations.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/operat.content:
# Completion for vault mutations

This is the single shared transaction contract for ordinary authorized vault
writes: capture, ingestion, original authoring, content repair, synthesis filing
and applied triage dispositions. Read-only search, answers, checks and previews
open no operations, logs, commits or refreshes. Purge retains its separate plan
and publication approvals and owns its transaction.

## Ownership and authorization

An authorized wiki edit includes scoped validation, catalog maintenance, log,
commit, sync and verified remote publication unless the user explicitly holds it.
Finish those steps without another routine permission question. Never create a
remote/repository just to satisfy publication. Without an upstream report local-only;
a local commit or closed token alone is not publication.

Read vault instructions. Preserve foreign edits and immutable raw bodies. A token
snapshots existing dirty paths, not later ownership, and does not isolate edits to
the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets. On resumption reconcile the saved
token, owned paths, log and actual commit before opening another operation; use
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md) for details.
Never delete a token or Git lock to hide unfinished work.

An enclosing operation may own delegated work. Give the worker that token; it
records exact paths and validation, never closes or aborts the parent's operation.
The named owner remains responsible for scoped publication. Do not close user-held
or foreign tokens. If blocked, retain actual state and a durable handoff naming
the token, owned files, completed steps, unfinished work and exact next action.

## Ordinary lifecycle

1. **Open before the first write.** Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op <op>` and retain the token.
   Create new pages only afterward. Use the existing operation vocabulary:
   original project documentation uses `relink`; derived answer filing uses `query`;
   discovery, ingestion, lint and relink retain their task operations.
2. **Keep an exact ledger.** Pass `--since <token>` to clippers, `log-entry.mjs`,
   `index-gen.mjs` and applied `refresh-catalogs.mjs` so they record actual written
   paths. Record file-tool edits with
   `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <vault-relative-path>...`. Use
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>` to produce the JSON array for
   `--paths-file`, under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. Inspect its warnings:
   pre-dirty recorded paths, paths no longer dirty and changed but unrecorded paths.
   Do not rebuild the ledger from Git's quoted filename display: Unicode paths
   can be silently lost. Unclaimed files are not automatically yours.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check behavior, schema, canonical placement and exact
   citations. Follow direct [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md)
   for changed pages and the relevant [checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md).
   Advance `reviewed` only after factual verification; mechanical edits preserve it.
   Inspect an uncertain write's actual target before retrying. A failed check
   stops completion until its cause is resolved within scope.
4. **Refresh affected owned catalogs once.** Generated fences are derived, never
   hand-edited. `index-gen.mjs` regenerates the global index while preserving manual
   framing. Project documentation uses [project catalogs](../../wiki-project/references/catalogs.md).
   A catalog already dirty from another writer remains theirs: use safe project
   generators and report deferred global refresh. Record actual changed paths,
   rebuild the ledger and rerun validation when the owned set grows.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative to
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token>`.
   The helper creates one unique `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md` with
   date/op/title metadata and records its path. Never append to an aggregate log.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Regenerate the ledger and read its warnings, then run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
   Never stage the whole vault. Verify actual path membership. A failed close
   retains the token. An unscoped close is refused whenever another token exists,
   of any age; there is no override. Pre-dirty paths require explicit ownership
   reconciliation; follow [close refusals](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#close-refusals).
   When receipts declare byte/hash integrity, pass their `--evidence-map <file>`;
   a mismatch must be resolved before completion, never ignored. The helper tries
   semantic index refresh after commit: inspect missing-backend/partial-build
   notices using [search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).
   A non-Git vault is local-only, not a successful Git commit.
7. **Sync and verify.** `op-commit` never pushes. Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"` after closing, not between
   edits. It fetches, rebases, pushes with one rejection retry and verifies against
   a fresh fetch. Inspect outgoing commits before publishing; coordinate unrelated
   or explicitly held local commits. Verify the operation's commit is included in
   upstream; after a rebase locate it through its unique log path and inspect the
   resulting path membership. Do not delegate publication to Obsidian Git or the user.
   Follow [sync recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#refused-sync)
   on failure; never force or guess at conflicts. `--commit-local` is for owned hand
   edits outside operations, refuses with any open token, and must not sweep foreign work.

## Combined close and publication

`wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<title>"` performs the
same scoped close, then normal sync and remote verification. It closes only the
given token and cannot combine with `--commit-local`. Without an explicit ledger
it uses recorded paths when available, else the guarded unscoped close; prefer an
explicit ledger, especially for file-tool edits. Success distinguishes the landed
commit and publication. A refused close pushes nothing and retains its token;
`committed, not published:` means the close landed and sync still needs recovery.
Inspect state and retry the unfinished step, not the content or log.

**Done only when** the requested change and owned catalogs are validated, one log
and the scoped operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is verified.
Report holds, local-only results and blockers precisely. Detailed verification,
refusal records, uncertain completion, cleanup and Git settings belong to
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md).

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh initialization can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

```sh
(
  export WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault'
  wiki_op_token=$(node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink) || exit
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since "$wiki_op_token" <path>...
  printf '%s\n' 'Validated task narrative' | node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" || exit
  wiki_ledger="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wiki-ledger-$wiki_op_token.json"
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since "$wiki_op_token" --out "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" --paths-file "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs' || exit
)
```

# Connect concepts and task maps

Read [access](access.md), [identity and relationships](efficacy.md),
[evidence](evidence.md) and [operation completion](operations.md). Read
[repair recipes](maintenance.md) only when a specific repair is indicated.

1. Inspect the requested navigation scope using the direct [health/topology check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog)
   and [identity/relationship checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#identity-and-relationship-checks).
   Unscored forward links and orphan/dead-end opportunities are not integrity
   obligations. Route actual integrity defects to [repair](repair.md) when
   authorized. A preview-only request stops after reports without an operation.
2. Before creating a page for a frequently mentioned entity, search candidate
   names and equivalent aliases; reuse the canonical page when it already exists.
   Never merge related concepts solely because names or embeddings are similar.
3. Obtain bounded candidates with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/relationships.mjs" --limit=10 --json`
   (optionally `--since=YYYY-MM-DD`, `--seed="wiki/concepts/<page>.md"`, or `--semantic`).
   Read both pages and their evidence. Choose a relationship role and explanatory
   sentence under the identity contract. Shared evidence and similarity do not
   establish equivalence or causality. Report accepted/rejected candidates and why.
4. Before an authorized write, open or reuse a **relink** operation. Record every
   edited page. Apply useful links under `## Relationships` within scope; seek
   input for uncertain interpretations. Keep supporting citations in `sources:`
   and factual prose, separate from navigation. Preserve `reviewed` on mechanical edits.
5. Build or refresh a small task MOC when it helps recurring questions: starting
   points, prerequisites, alternatives, complementary domains and open questions.
   Use `_templates/task-map.md`; keep generated document catalogs distinct. Use
   [project guidance](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md) for original
   project pages, and its [catalog procedure](../../wiki-project/references/catalogs.md)
   for project-generated navigation.
6. Confirm new links resolve and a task query can retrieve the map. Follow direct
   [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md), then finish one
   relink log, scoped ledger/commit, sync and remote verification through
   [operations](operations.md). Inspect actual paths and index notices; a local
   commit alone is not publication.

**Done:** relationships are explained and supported, canonical identity is
preserved, affected maps are findable, and authorized changes have verified
completion. A preview remains read-only.
