# Advanced retrieval and evidence routes

Use the [simple search workflow](../SKILL.md#simple-search) for root resolution,
bounded lookup and passage reading. This reference adds retrieval choices; every
step is read-only. Diagnostics and repair recipes live in
[search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).

## Scope and disambiguation

Use `--json --limit=10` for bounded passages and metadata: project/type/status,
factual review dates, provenance targets and index freshness. Add
`--project=<slug>`, `--type=<type>` or `--status=<state>` only when the question
establishes scope. Page status (`draft`/`maintained`) is not a backlog lifecycle;
use [backlog listing](../../wiki-project/references/backlog.md#list-by-lifecycle)
for planned or startable work.

Exact titles and equivalent aliases are prioritized. Open all plausible full
paths when a title is ambiguous; compare the scope, context and requested project.
An alias names an equivalent concept, not any similarly worded topic. When a
question needs several terms, run a small set of complementary bounded queries
and report their coverage. Do not hide complementary domains with an arbitrary
filter. Check decision/backlog metadata before calling a proposal shipped.

## Explicit raw lookup

`wiki/` is the synthesized index; immutable `raw/` evidence is excluded from the
keyword default and semantic index. Request raw lookup explicitly:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "useful terms" --include-raw --json --limit=10
```

Raw hits are appended after normal wiki results rather than blended into the
fused ranking. Report the actual raw hit count, including zero, **only if the raw
scan succeeded**. A `raw/ clippings NOT searched` diagnostic or failed raw channel
means missing coverage, never zero evidence. Use the supported helper before a
bounded filesystem fallback. Exclude `.recycle/`, hidden folders and binary originals.

Read the actual raw passage and its fidelity/restriction metadata before quoting
or using it as support. A raw hit is unvetted evidence; a route to it is not proof
of the claim. Apply the direct [evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md),
including quarantined/retired restrictions and Reddit/Medium separation.

## Follow provenance

Resolve a returned wiki citation to its raw evidence:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs" "wiki/sources/Example.md:23"
```

The helper strips a `:line` suffix; an explicit raw path is already evidence.
It also accepts search output on stdin:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "useful terms" | node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs"
```

Open the returned paths and verify the exact supporting text. `unreachable`
means the citation trail does not reach raw evidence, not permission to invent a
source. `declared-no-provenance` distinguishes original authored pages declaring
`sources: []` from broken derived provenance. Retain unresolved citations in the
coverage report. Original project facts may be grounded in verified behavior;
do not demand a fabricated clipping for first-party documentation.

## Read the result honestly

Inspect stderr plus JSON `channels`, `diagnostics`, `indexFreshness` and
`semanticGate`. Hybrid is a channel state, not a relevance guarantee. Lexical
results are real without semantic ranking; a failed primary wiki scan means
incomplete coverage even if MOCs or semantic results answer. Candidate validation
can be bounded, so disclose relevant candidate-limit notices. Open current files:
modified semantic hits are excluded until refreshed and removed hits are dropped;
live lexical/identity matches can still have outdated embeddings.

For an answer spanning sources, load [cited answers](answers.md) directly. For a
requested diagnosis load [search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).
Neither path authorizes backend installs or index rebuilds.

skills/wiki-search/references/answers.md.content:
# Answer with citations

This workflow synthesizes a response from retrieved passages and never files it.
Read [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before quoting or
synthesizing. Use [advanced retrieval](advanced.md) when scope, raw evidence or
provenance traversal is needed; the main [simple search](../SKILL.md#simple-search)
procedure suffices for ordinary lookup.

1. Run bounded searches for the question and useful alternative wording. Include
   raw only when the question calls for evidence that may be unprocessed. Read
   channel diagnostics and disclose degraded or failed coverage, including the
   raw count when successfully searched.
2. Open canonical pages, relevant alternatives and supporting evidence. Inspect
   factual review dates, page scope and decision/backlog states. A proposed ADR
   or planned feature is not current behavior. Verify citation routes with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs" "wiki/sources/Example.md:23"`,
   then read the resolved raw passage; a reachable route alone proves no claim.
3. For cross-topic questions, use [identity and relationships](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md)
   and verify explained relationships against evidence. Similar neighbors are not
   causal evidence. Label connections inferred across sources as the wiki's synthesis.
4. Write a cited answer distinguishing established source claims, disagreement,
   unsupported claims and inference. Preserve restrictions when reusing summaries.
   Place Reddit-derived claims under `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and
   Medium-derived material under `## Medium articles`, outside the opening summary,
   main factual sections and recommendations. Independently supported facts may
   use their higher-quality citations in the main answer.
5. Report what the searches did and did not cover. A clipping's silence establishes
   “not supported here,” never “false.” Disclose partial capture or uncertain
   character fidelity before quoting. Do not transform a zero-hit result into a
   claim that no relevant knowledge exists.

**Done:** the answer has usable path/line citations to passages actually opened,
source claims and inference are distinguished, and vault files remain unchanged.

If the user explicitly authorizes filing, hand original documentation to
[wiki-project](../../wiki-project/SKILL.md) or a provenance-derived synthesis to
[maintainer synthesis filing](../../wiki-maintainer/references/synthesis-filing.md).
The receiving writer owns the operation; answering alone never opens one.

skills/wiki-search/SKILL.md.content:
---
name: wiki-search
description: Use when asked to find wiki pages or passages, look up a title or alias, search captured evidence, trace provenance, or answer a question from the wiki with citations. Read-only retrieval; original project documentation belongs to wiki-project, diagnostics to wiki-setup, and external discovery or ingestion to wiki-researcher.
---

# Search and answer from the wiki

Find relevant passages and explain what they support. This skill never writes
content, opens an operation, logs, commits or refreshes indexes. A question does
not authorize filing its answer or researching new sources.

## Simple search

1. Resolve the installed plugin root from this `SKILL.md`: two parents above its
   containing skill folder. Resolve the known vault from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT`,
   default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` requires an
   explicit vault. Before the first helper, open/read the actual vault `AGENTS.md`
   if present; do not infer its contents from helper output or a host plugin name.
   Use that root, not a recursive profile or whole-vault inventory. No running app
   is required.
2. Replace the placeholder below with the quoted absolute installed root and run
   one bounded query. If changing the vault for a command, restore the prior
   environment afterward; [shell examples](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md#shell-portability)
   are optional when needed.

   ```sh
   node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "exact title or useful terms" --json --limit=10
   ```

   The default content scopes are `wiki/` and `moc/`; raw evidence is opt-in.
3. Read stderr status and JSON coverage metadata. Disclose lexical-only search
   and failed channels, including failures inside a hybrid run. Missing/stale
   indexes or zero hits do not establish that the vault knows nothing. A failed
   raw channel means **not searched**, not zero evidence.
4. Open each useful result's exact path under the vault at its matched line and
   read surrounding passages. Verify relevance, page status, review date and
   decision/backlog state. A planned feature or proposed ADR is not shipped.
   Disambiguate similar titles by full path and context instead of guessing.
5. Return useful page paths with line citations and a concise account of what
   the passages support, including missing coverage. For a narrative answer or
   quotation, read the directly linked [cited-answer procedure](references/answers.md)
   and [evidence policy](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).

**Example.** Request: “Find the Beacon deployment guide.” Action: search
`"Beacon deployment"`, open the matched guide passage and check its title/scope.
Result: “The deployment steps are in `wiki/authored/beacon/guides/deployment.md:24`;
this run used lexical search, so semantic ranking contributed nothing.” Use the
actual path, line and channel result, never the example as evidence.

## Advanced search

Read [advanced retrieval](references/advanced.md) for scoped or multi-query
retrieval, exact-title/alias ambiguity, explicit raw evidence and provenance walks.
For questions spanning claims or sources, also read [cited answers](references/answers.md),
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) and, when relationships matter,
[identity and relationships](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

**Example.** Request: “Does Beacon already support two workers? Include the raw
evidence.” Action: search with `--project=beacon --include-raw --json --limit=10`,
open the architecture and planned backlog passages, resolve their evidence routes,
then check the actual raw text. Result: a cited distinction between deployed and
proposed behavior, with the raw-hit count or an explicit failed-coverage statement.

**Example.** Request: “What do these sources agree on?” Action: run complementary
bounded queries, open the supporting passages and preserve contradictory evidence.
Result: a cited answer separating source claims from the wiki's inference; nothing
is filed by this skill.

## Best practices and handoffs

- Prefer exact titles and equivalent aliases, then useful terms. Use a scope only
  when the request establishes it. Read passages rather than trusting ranking.
- Keep filesystem fallback bounded to `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/`
  only for requested evidence. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`, dot folders,
  dependencies or binary originals.
- For a requested diagnosis, use [search diagnostics](../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md).
  A degraded lookup never authorizes repair or installation.
- For project work listed by lifecycle, use [backlog listing](../wiki-project/references/backlog.md#list-by-lifecycle).
- If writing is explicitly authorized, hand original documentation to
  [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md), and provenance-derived synthesis filing
  to [maintainer filing](../wiki-maintainer/references/synthesis-filing.md). Do not
  perform the write from this read-only workflow.
- New external discovery/capture/ingestion requires its own requested scope in
  [wiki-researcher](../wiki-researcher/SKILL.md); a search miss is not authorization.

## Done

The requested lookup or answer has opened supporting passages, usable citations,
honest coverage limits and no vault changes. If nothing supports the claim, say
“not found by these queries” and name the queries; do not invent an answer.

skills/wiki-setup/references/app-access..content:
# App access and session diagnosis

Use [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) for the canonical root,
supported channels and guarded-action policy. The app is needed for app actions;
filesystem reads, checks and ordinary Markdown edits work from the known vault
root. Diagnosis does not authorize a content repair or an app mutation.

## Resolve the requested app surface

1. Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`) without scanning
   the user profile. Resolve the app name from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT_NAME` or the
   vault folder basename. These are distinct values.
2. For an app-only action, use the guarded helper at its installed absolute path:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" vault info=path` can confirm
   the responding app's vault root. The known filesystem root does not depend
   on this probe. `vaults` lists registered vaults when app registration needs checking.
3. Read `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" help <command>` when
   a parameter seems unsupported; the live command's help outranks a stale
   syntax description. The [native action reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/obsidian-cli.md)
   owns supported actions and their authorization workflow.

Node.js 20.8 or newer is required by the guarded transport. App registration is
separate from filesystem initialization: open the intended folder as an
Obsidian vault and verify it through the helper when that setup is requested.
A successful filesystem health report does not prove app access.

## Windows invocation

Never call bare `obsidian` from Git Bash. Obsidian's `.com` terminal redirector
connects stdin/stdout to the GUI app. PowerShell and Node's `execFileSync` use
PATHEXT ordering to select it; Git Bash can select `.exe`, print nothing and
exit 0. Use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs"` through the
supported host. A GUI process exiting successfully is not a valid empty result.
The guard is part of the supported access path; do not bypass it with a direct
native call even when diagnosing the redirector.

## Empty output: one lazy canary

Do not preflight every ordinary app read. A command returning results has
already established a live backend for that session. Only when an empty result
is about to decide something (such as no backlinks or skipping a page), and
the session has not yet established liveness, run:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="the" total
```

A numeric response establishes liveness; trust that empty and later empties
without repeating the probe. An empty canary is unavailable backend coverage,
not a count of zero. Obsidian provides no documented no-results exit contract.
Do not infer an index rebuild from empty output. A stopped-app failure can
explicitly say the CLI cannot find Obsidian; report the observed failure rather
than promising the command will launch it.

## Failure, refusal and uncertain mutation

Keep the exact diagnostic and distinguish what was sent:

| Result | Next action |
|---|---|
| `CLI_REQUEST`, `CLI_BUSY`, `CLI_LOCK` | Request was not sent. Narrow an oversized read or use the supported filesystem channel. Do not disable the guard or split a note into repeated CLI writes. |
| App unavailable | Report which app-only action could not run. Continue independent filesystem work; do not loop waiting or require an app restart for it. |
| Command timeout or worker failure | A mutation may have run. Read the exact target and reconcile the intended effect before retrying or switching to filesystem editing. An app-only effect cannot be claimed from a filesystem approximation. |
| Process death released the guard | This does not prove its child or submitted app mutation finished. Inspect the uncertain target as above. |

The wrapper never automatically retries. Within one Node process, await
asynchronous CLI work before using the synchronous adapter so the event loop
can release its gate. Existing older callers or direct native commands are not
protected by updating this plugin; the guard is not machine-wide interception.
See the [public transport contract](../../../docs/cli-transport-guards.md) for
the exact enforced request and wait limits. Keep the existing operation and use
[operation recovery](operation-recovery.md) if a requested write was interrupted.

## Triage UI reachability and session recovery

The [triage workflow](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md) owns showing
the queue and applying the user's dispositions. The helper returns a tokenized
`link` and a clean `url`: give the user `link`; opening `url` alone returns 401.
The browser then uses an HttpOnly cookie lasting 30 days. Starting the queue
creates local session state, not tracked content; it does not authorize applying
dispositions.

The per-vault session directory is `.wiki-master/triage-ui/`; rerunning refreshes
the existing server instead of creating another, and it idles out after 30
minutes. For a lost link, reuse the token in `state/token` (gitignored,
machine-local, mode `0600`) and remembered `state/port`; do not rotate them as a
routine fix. The stable port avoids invalidating the host/port cookie scope.
Only for an explicitly requested rotation, remove that exact token file and
rerun the triage helper; all existing cookies then stop working.

Remote triage uses the requested workflow's `--remote` option: it binds every
interface and advertises a reachable address rather than `0.0.0.0`. Uploads
remain on the server's disk. `WM_TRIAGE_URL_HOST` overrides an advertised host
that the user's browser cannot reach; change it only within the setup scope.
Plain LAN transport exposes the token in cleartext; use a trusted tailnet or
HTTPS front when the network is untrusted. Never publish the token into logs,
source files or diagnostic transcripts.

skills/wiki-setup/references/capture-pre.content:
# Capture prerequisites and diagnosis

Use only the section for the source being captured. Resolve the installed helper
root and vault through [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md).
Prerequisite probes and diagnosis do not authorize installs, authentication
changes, captures, re-clips or ingestion. Report what is unavailable and its
effect on coverage; never substitute invented evidence. Before an authorized
capture or repair writes, follow [operations](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
The [evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) owns restrictions,
raw immutability and the obligations for using captured material.

## HTML and supplied pages

The public HTML helper is `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs"`.
It uses the pinned extraction dependencies; a source checkout installs them with
`npm ci`, while installed plugins acquire the pinned versions through npm exec
when local dependencies are absent. Installation is a setup action, not a search
or diagnostic side effect. See the [public extraction contract](../../../docs/clipping-fidelity.md)
for extractor behavior, and [capture](../../wiki-researcher/references/capture.md)
for the authorized write procedure.

Interpret an actual result before choosing a recovery:

| Observation | Diagnosis and next action |
|---|---|
| Fetched `thin content` | The extraction may be a SPA or paywall; the automatic decline prevents blind retries. Have the user supply the saved page and use the capture route's `--from-file`, with `--override-decline` only for an automatic decline. |
| `wrong-node` | Login, consent or age-gate content is queued, not declined. A signed-in saved page can supply the actual content; do not call a wall a verdict on the source. |
| `failed` (for example 403/network) | Transient failure is queued, not auto-declined. Report it; a retry needs capture scope and evidence that retrying is useful. |
| `gone` | A dead/404/error-page source needs a replacement source or dropped claim; do not label it a retryable `failed` row. |
| `clash` | Nothing was written; an attention row names the occupied path. Read that file's `source:` and choose a distinct `--slug=<name>` within capture scope, or leave it for triage. A clash is not a same-URL duplicate. |
| `duplicate` / `unchanged` | No new content was written. A new dated capture of changed HTML uses `--recapture`; this flag does not exist on document, GitHub or Confluence clippers. |
| Partial fidelity warning | Inspect the source items the checker says were lost; a clipping's length does not establish completeness. Its `quality` is credibility, not extraction fidelity. |

For a supplied page, verify it is the intended page before capture. Accepted
extensions are `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.html` and `.htm`; an empty path,
missing file, directory or other extension exits 2 before writing or queuing.
Files over 1 MiB, binary/NUL data or sufficiently undecodable text are refused
and queued as attention. Thin supplied pages are queued, never automatically
declined; a short structured page can pass the helper's heading/word exception.
There is no override for the login/consent/age-gate classifier. It cannot judge a
title with no word of at least five letters (such as a bare numeric URL suffix),
so a successful run is not proof that a supplied file is the real page.

An `extraction: manual` clipping is refused by `apply-reclips.mjs`, not counted
as a failed repair. To refresh it, obtain the newly saved page and use the
capture route's `--from-file <path> --recapture`. Never replace its supplied
body with a fresh unauthenticated fetch. A raw text URL is handled as plaintext;
HTML repair does not re-read plaintext clippings. See
[re-clipping](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for the supported repair API.

## PDF

Run the read-only toolchain probe before a PDF capture:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" --doctor
```

It probes the external tools and reports what each missing tool costs; the
clipper also reports degraded prerequisites on each capture. Missing `pdftotext`
is fatal. Xpdf is preferred because its `-table` mode preserves reconstructed
row pairings; poppler lacks it. Missing `pdftoppm` or Tesseract prevents OCR of
scanned pages. An `ocr-unavailable` result means the PDF was not read and creates
no decline; a `thin` result means extraction and available OCR could not recover
useful content and records a decline. Do not treat those outcomes alike.

The clipper invokes tools through Node's `execFileSync`; use the bundled helper
instead of a Bash invocation that may resolve Windows executables incorrectly.
If an installation is authorized, the [Xpdf tools](https://www.xpdfreader.com/download.html)
provide `-table`; OCR needs `pdftoppm` and Tesseract. Do not install them merely
because a diagnostic request found them missing.

For figure capture, `pdftoppm` renders pages; `pdfimages`, `pdftocairo` and
`pdfinfo` support selection/probing. They are found on PATH or in the winget
poppler folder. Missing optional probes produce warnings and `auto` uses the
probes available. A successful text clip does not prove figures were captured.
The [PDF capture procedure](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-pdf.md) owns
figure selection, caps, sidecars and hash checks.

### Wrong reading mode or garbled text

Inspect the extraction against the PDF. Reading order suits prose, two-column
papers and body-plus-margin layouts. Aligned table mode suits real tables;
using it on margin annotations can splice unrelated text into a body line.
Conversely, reading order can emit all keys followed by all values, losing row
pairings. Neither mode is correct merely because the output looks like prose.

For a bounded comparison, extract a couple of pages both ways using the resolved
converter through Node (replace the page numbers and converter path):

```sh
node -e "const {execFileSync}=require('node:child_process'); process.stdout.write(execFileSync(process.argv[1], ['-enc','UTF-8','-f','40','-l','41',process.argv[2],'-']));" "<absolute-pdftotext-path>" "<file.pdf>"
node -e "const {execFileSync}=require('node:child_process'); process.stdout.write(execFileSync(process.argv[1], ['-enc','UTF-8','-f','40','-l','41','-table',process.argv[2],'-']));" "<absolute-pdftotext-path>" "<file.pdf>"
```

The existing capture flags are `--mode=auto|reading-order|table`. An override
diverging from the detector warns and records `reading-order-forced` when
applicable. Invalid modes fail; forcing `table` without `-table` support is
refused, never silently downgraded. `--ocr` forces OCR for broken font layers;
`--ocr-lang=<code>` selects its language (default `eng`). Use an authorized
capture/repair route for the write, not a diagnostic run.

Read fidelity markers as limits: `table-flattened` lost the rows and cannot
support pairings; `tabular` reconstructed them; `ocr` has unverified recognized
words/numbers; `degraded` cannot support unverified verbatim spans. Reassessment
cannot prove OCR or table layout from characters and must not clear those floors.
For a read-only legacy inventory:

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --ocr-floor
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-fidelity.mjs" --inventory
```

`--ocr-floor --apply` is an authorized metadata repair, not diagnosis. It adds
the floor to old OCR captures; it does not verify their content. Broken-font
inventory only lists old captures newly detected as suspect. Actual repairs and
derived-claim review belong to [maintainer](../../wiki-maintainer/SKILL.md).

## Word

The [Word route](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-docx.md) uses
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs"`. Probe pandoc with
`pandoc -v` in PowerShell, or invoke its resolved executable through Node on
Windows. A missing converter requires [pandoc installation](https://pandoc.org/installing.html)
within authorized setup scope; stop capture rather than inventing text.

A corrupt or password-protected document fails for manual handling. `thin`
does not distinguish a bad extraction from an intentionally brief worksheet:
open the original and inspect completeness before using the capture route's
`--allow-short`. Its normal floor is 100 words. Never use the override to push
through unreadable content. Pandoc's plain-text output loses table/figure
structure; clean Unicode does not establish faithful structure.

## PowerPoint

The [PowerPoint route](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-pptx.md) uses
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pptx.mjs"` and bundled Python glue.
Probe the same interpreters in order and stop at the first success:

```sh
python3 -c "import pptx"
python -c "import pptx"
py -c "import pptx"
```

On Windows `python3` may be a failing WindowsApps alias even when another
interpreter has python-pptx. Failure of that first probe alone proves nothing
about the library. If all fail, identify the interpreter that will run the
helper and report `<interpreter> -m pip install python-pptx` as the needed setup
action; installing into another interpreter will not fix it. Pandoc has no
PowerPoint input format; LibreOffice is not this helper's dependency.

Legacy binary `.ppt` is unsupported and must be converted to `.pptx` first.
Empty/corrupt/protected decks need manual handling. Extracted text, tables and
speaker notes omit design, images and rendered charts; inspect those limits
against the deck before describing the capture as complete.

## Spreadsheets

The [spreadsheet route](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-xlsx.md) uses
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs"`. Probe both `soffice
--version` and `pandoc -v` through PowerShell or Node on Windows. The helper
invokes bare `soffice` through Node so PATHEXT selects the `.com` console shim;
the `.exe` GUI build can print nothing. Do not route this through Bash.
Missing [LibreOffice](https://www.libreoffice.org/download/) is a fatal setup
defect; a corrupt/protected workbook returns `failed` and permits a batch to
continue. Report which occurred.

Never convert a workbook to PDF to work around missing converters: it can lose
the label/value pairing that is the content. The supported path renders every
sheet as a table, but formulas, merged cells, charts and multi-row headers can
lose meaning. Verify labels remain attached to values against the workbook.
A `thin` result (under 100 words) records a decline. There is no `--allow-short`
flag here; report the limit and seek a supported source/capture decision rather
than claiming the tiny workbook succeeded or retyping its cells into raw.

## GitHub repositories

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-gh.mjs" --doctor
```

This checks the `gh` CLI and authentication. Capture uses the existing `gh auth`
session through `gh repo clone`, including private repos already accessible to
that account. Missing access, a bad repository name and network failure are
capture failures, not permission to change credentials or fabricate files.
See the [GitHub route](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-gh.md) for per-file
and digest capture.

`too-many-files` occurs only with `--force-full`: no content was written.
Within requested capture scope, increase `--max-files` deliberately or remove
`--force-full` to let digest mode bound output. A changed digest grouping can
prune obsolete listings; inspect reported paths and verify listing totals
against the manifest. Do not mistake a listing for captured file contents.
Unsafe or doubled legacy names require the maintainer's
[citation-preserving repair](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md),
not a hand rename during diagnosis.

## Confluence

```sh
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" --doctor
```

The optional `confluencer` plugin supplies authenticated `page.mjs`; wiki-master
does not implement another client. Discovery searches Copilot plugin installs
for the external confluencer helper `page.mjs` in that plugin's `scripts` directory. For another host or development checkout,
set `WIKI_MASTER_CONFLUENCER_SCRIPTS` to its absolute scripts directory for the
command's scope and restore the prior value afterwards. The doctor reports
discovery and delegates auth/config/connectivity checks to confluencer's own
`doctor.mjs`; do not print or independently handle its credentials.

`confluencer-missing` reports the paths searched and override, with no clipping.
If found but failing, the helper surfaces the real `page.mjs` stderr and doctor
pointer. Report bad ID/auth/network failures accurately. An anonymous HTML fetch
usually sees a login wall or SPA shell and cannot replace authenticated access.

Within authorized setup scope, install/configure confluencer if desired. A
user-supplied export can instead go through the matching Word or PDF capture
route, with an explicit table-fidelity caveat. Do not hand-write raw Markdown.
PDF export is a double lossy conversion and does not repair server-side Jira
macro errors. The native [Confluence capture route](../../wiki-researcher/references/clip-confluence.md)
retains the page's own URL, version and update metadata.

Confluence's stable URL dedup does not notice a newer page version: a re-clip can
return `duplicate (already clipped)`. No version-aware dedup or `--recapture`
flag is supplied for this helper. Report that limitation; never remove old raw
evidence or invent a flag to bypass it.

skills/wiki-setup/references/checks.md.content:
# Report health, freshness and content findings

Resolve the known vault and absolute helpers through
[access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Read-only reports open no
operation and write no log, disposition, catalog or cache. Follow
[evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) when reviewing claims;
structural checks cannot establish truth.

## Health and ingest backlog

1. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`. Use `--json` for versioned
   issues with stable IDs, exact locations, evidence and verification conditions.
2. Report uncapped open integrity defects with scanned-page coverage. Intentional
   forward links, orphan/dead-end opportunities and stubs do not increase that
   count. Required citations remain required on stubs. Age, unresolved navigation
   and fuzzy suggestions do not establish an accidental break. Empty coverage
   cannot justify a healthy-wiki verdict.
3. Use `health.mjs --backlog` for ingestion counts; this does not process captures.
   The canonical [hash-join contract](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md#has-this-been-ingested--a-content-hash-join-not-a-guess)
   determines eligibility. Do not invent a filename/title join.

| Metric | Interpretation and next action |
|---|---|
| `unparsedSources` | No wiki page cites the clipping; distinct from summarized state. |
| `unsummarizedSources` | No source summary records its hash: the ingestion backlog. |
| `missingHash` | Markdown clipping lacks `source-hash`; a capture/data defect. |
| `backfillPending` | Legacy summary lacks hashes; transitional link credit is active, migration has not run. |
| `provenanceGaps` | Source page cites no raw file; structural defect, not proof that the claim is false. |

Only Markdown clippings are ingestable units; PDF/spreadsheet/ZIP originals are
not summary targets. Report `unsummarizedSources` when asked how much remains.
For authorized repairs use [maintenance recipes](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md)
or [repair](../../wiki-maintainer/references/repair.md); for requested ingestion use
[wiki-researcher](../../wiki-researcher/SKILL.md).

The old capped score and topology counts are available only through `--legacy`
for historical comparison. They are not repair targets. Compare resolved,
remaining and new issue IDs after an authorized repair. Zero defects does not
prove factual accuracy. [Integrity contracts](../../../docs/wiki-integrity.md)
describe structural coverage and unchecked areas.

The `monolith candidates` line flags authored pages over roughly 3,000 words with
several stacked dated-update callouts; it is a review signal, not permission to
rewrite. Follow [project authoring](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md)
when a living-document repair is authorized.

## Freshness and drift coverage

1. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/stale.mjs"`. Read the backend diagnostic:
   failed, invalid or empty CLI discovery falls back to scoped `wiki/` files.
   Missing root/wiki is failure, not an empty report.
2. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/drift.mjs" --coverage`. This reads
   evaluation coverage; it does not run embeddings. Do not run cache-producing
   embedding evaluation for a strict read-only request.
3. Separate stale pages, missing factual-review dates, evaluated coverage and
   failures. Prioritize use and volatility. `reviewed` means factual verification;
   `updated` means edited; refreshed embeddings do not make claims reviewed.
4. A request about whether recommendations still hold needs actual claim and
   evidence inspection through [cited answers](../../wiki-search/references/answers.md).
   Report which claims were checked and which remain unverified. A sample is not
   a whole-wiki verdict; zero evaluated is not “no drift.”

## Content lint report

Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lint.mjs"` for warn-only findings,
`--json` for the full list. Scope to requested work using `--page=<substr>`,
`--updated-since=<YYYY-MM-DD>` or `--paths-file=<ledger>`; date and ledger may be
combined. The graph is still whole-vault; scope saves quote checks, not graph scan.
Use `--tier=convention|gapped|unverified`, `--full` for untruncated quotations,
`--ids` for finding identities and `--include-reviewed` for prior dispositions.
These reporting options do not record new verdicts.

- **convention:** same words and order, markup/punctuation/extraction spacing
  differs. Counted rather than listed; inspect unusual jumps instead of assuming
  a new factual problem.
- **gapped:** every quoted word occurs in evidence order, with additional evidence
  words between. Inspect inserted runs: timestamps/headers/citations may be
  extraction noise; omitted clauses or joined sentences may need correction.
- **unverified:** changed, added, reordered or negated words, dropped operators,
  or missing evidence text. `--near` shows diffs for quotations of six or more
  words aligning with raw at 0.85 or better: `[-word-]` is page-only, `{+word+}` is
  clipping-only. A typo correction may be benign; a changed meaning is not. A
  low match is no proof of error. Two-column interleaving can also trigger this.

Read a bounded sample and the exact evidence trail before judging quotations.
Check ambiguous/misrouted citations first. Distinguish own wording, mention/title
quotes, retracted claims, real drift and unsupported claims. Style flags are
review pointers, not scored violations. The
[content-lint contract](../../../README.md#content-lint) describes mark pairing
(curly marks nest; straight marks alternate) and skipped style spans.

Report evaluated findings and remaining uncertainty. A reporting request never
runs `lint-disposition.mjs record` or edits dates/content. Authorized factual
corrections and persisted dispositions use [maintainer lint](../../wiki-maintainer/references/lint.md).
Keep clipping fidelity distinct from source credibility and apply evidence restrictions.

## Identity and relationship checks

For suspected naming ambiguity run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/identity-audit.mjs" --json`. Apply the shared
[identity policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md); a warning is a
review queue, not permission to merge/rename. Candidate relationships use
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/relationships.mjs" --limit=10 --json`.
Read both pages and their evidence; shared sources or semantic neighbors prove
neither equivalence nor causality. Adding links belongs to authorized maintainer work.

## Bounded maintenance evaluation

During requested substantive maintenance, start with health and stop for an empty
wiki. A clean graph still needs bounded review of changed/high-use pages. Run
drift `--coverage` first, then `drift.mjs --limit=10` only when the maintenance
scope permits its machine-local embedding cache. Report eligible, evaluated,
skipped and failed counts, document/chunk sampling and backend failures. Cosine
drift measures topical change, never truth or contradiction. A page evaluated
through sampled chunks has not received an exhaustive factual review.

Open the content owner's operation only before an authorized tracked edit.
Do not run full lint on an unchanged wiki; use scoped checks and inspect actual
claims rather than optimizing a graph score. Validate changed paths through
[scoped validation](validation.md), then complete the owner's operation.

## Verification cadence

- Each ingest or substantive edit checks identity and citation paths, updates
  affected task maps and completes the operation; factual dates follow evidence.
- Each requested maintenance pass combines structural defects with bounded
  changed/high-use claim review, reporting evaluated/skipped/failed coverage.
- While actively growing, a weekly review of up to ten relationship candidates,
  high-demand stubs and discovery gaps is useful guidance, not an installed schedule.
- After search/schema changes, and periodically as vocabulary changes, run the
  retrieval regression set, inspect development failures, then measure held-out
  queries without tuning to them. Report categories, not one misleading score.

See [efficacy command contracts](../../../docs/wiki-efficacy.md) for evaluation
interfaces. Setup owns these checks; repairs and source-writing remain with their
task owners.

## Purge broken-link verification

Before any authorized purge mutation, retain
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --legacy` and its **broken links**
count. Run the same check after applying the purge and repairing collateral; the
count must not grow. Report before/after values and actual coverage.

Neither a better legacy score nor the default integrity defect count substitutes
for this comparison. The score can improve when removed pages stop contributing
orphan penalties, while dangling navigation to deleted targets remains unscored.
Inspect collateral pages directly. When native access is already available,
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" unresolved verbose format=json`
also attributes unresolved links to their source pages; app access is not required
for the filesystem check.

This diagnostic procedure never applies, restores or reconciles a purge. Those
mutations and publication approvals belong to the [purge workflow](../../wiki-purge/references/purge.md).

# Initialize a new vault safely

Read [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) and
[operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) before
initializing. Resolve the explicit intended root and scoped environment. Never
initialize a guessed directory or create a Git repository/remote just to publish.

## Preflight existing files

Inspect the intended root's existing `AGENTS.md`, schema, index and `_templates/`.
`init.mjs` preserves existing root index/schema/base files, but its recursive
template copy can overwrite same-named files under `_templates/`. Its generic
“existing files are kept” help is not a guarantee for customized templates.

For a new root or one with no template collisions, continue. If templates already
exist, compare them against the installed `templates/_templates/` before running
init. Identical collisions are safe; differing/customized collisions require a
non-overwriting plan. Do not run init over those templates or temporarily move
them out of the way merely to restore them later. Report the exact collisions
and preserve them; if the request authorizes completing the partial scaffold,
create only missing folders/files from the bundled templates under the same
operation, leaving every existing file unchanged. Record those exact new paths.
Do not claim that the helper provided an overwrite-safe mode; it has none.

## Initialize and verify

1. Open an operation **before** scaffolding:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op relink`.
   The fresh-vault exception allows its state directory to exist before the other
   folders. Retain the token and owned-path ledger.
2. With no differing template collisions, run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/init.mjs"`. If authorized to complete a
   partial scaffold with customized collisions, use the missing-only copy path
   described above **instead of running init**, and preserve every existing file.
   **`init.mjs` does not record an operation ledger.** Compare the preflight file
   list with the resulting files, then explicitly record every newly written file:

   ```sh
   node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <each-new-vault-relative-file>
   ```

   Include new root files (`index.md`, `log.md`, `.gitignore`, `vault-schema.md`,
   `stale.base`, `log.base`) and every new `_templates/` file, not just authored
   pages or the eventual log. Record actual files, not directories or files that
   were already present and unchanged. Inspect expected `raw/clippings`, wiki
   content folders, `moc`, `log`, `_templates`, schema, index and bases. Confirm
   prior content bytes are unchanged; distinguish scaffold success from app registration.
3. Run the direct [health check](checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog). Empty content
   is expected in a new vault; report scan scope instead of claiming factual health.
   Validate any authored pages this task additionally created using
   [scoped validation](validation.md).
4. Write one relink log with `--since <token>`, then run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`.
   **Inspect that ledger before closing:** every scaffold file written in step 2
   and the log must be present, including in a non-Git vault. Resolve unclaimed
   owned files with `op-ledger.mjs add`; do not assume initialization auto-recorded
   them or let a log-only ledger stand for the scaffold. Close through
   `op-commit.mjs --op relink --since <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "Initialize vault"`.
   Without Git, report local-only initialization. With an existing configured
   upstream and no explicit hold, complete ordinary sync/remote verification.
   Do not leave a token open simply because no Git repository exists.
5. Relay one-time app setup separately: open the folder as an Obsidian vault,
   verify `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" vaults`, and import
   `templates/webclipper-template.json` into Web Clipper. Use
   [app access](app-access.md) if requested app setup fails. Filesystem health
   does not prove the native CLI reaches the app.

**Done:** expected files exist, prior content is preserved, the initialization
operation is accounted for and publication/local-only state is explicit. If
customized template collisions prevent safe progress, report them without mutation.

skills/wiki-setup/references/operation-r.content:
# Diagnose and recover operation failures

Read [operation ownership and completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
before any authorized recovery. A diagnostic request inspects state only. Keep
the saved token, ledger, log path and actual commit state; never restart blindly.

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Apply the shared [ownership contract](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md#ownership-and-authorization); do not close a foreign or held token.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

## Abandoned tokens

 List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

## Stopping early

 A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

## Refused sync

 `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

## Refusal record

 Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

## Git ownership

 The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
vault's `vault-schema.md` (written during initialization) carries the same statement; an existing
vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.

**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.

## Close refusals

A ledger path that
   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
   same file.
   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.

## Sync verification and failures

A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.

## Combined completion results and open-operation notices

   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.

   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.


## Interrupted purge

The [purge workflow](../../wiki-purge/references/purge.md) owns approval, seeds,
manifest and publication. Recovery never widens an approved plan.

`--apply` reports the files it could not move and **stops before committing**. The
usual cause is a Windows file lock — antivirus mid-scan, the Search indexer, a sync
client holding a read-only handle.

Close whatever holds them open, then run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/purge.mjs" --reconcile`. It finishes this purge in
place, into the same bin folder, and commits.

**Do not re-run `--apply`.** The seed pages are already gone, so its plan comes back
empty; it starts a *second* purge under a new id, writes a manifest with no entries,
and commits something that claims a purge and contains none — while the real
half-purge stays uncommitted and gets reported back as the user's own work.


## Purge history connectivity

Before purge mutation, run the following against the actual configured vault and
upstream, using scoped Git reads rather than assuming a branch name:

```sh
git -C "<vault>" fetch
git -C "<vault>" merge-base HEAD "<configured-upstream>"
```

A failed fetch or missing upstream is a distinct failure, not proof of unrelated
histories. A non-Git vault has no history to compare and is local-only. If Git
confirms there is no merge base, stop: a locally successful purge cannot reach
other machines on an unrelated lineage. Choosing which history is canonical is
outside purge authorization; never force or invent a reconciliation.

The [purge workflow](../../wiki-purge/references/purge.md) retains the obligation
to perform this check and owns approval, removal and publication. Fetch/history
diagnosis does not authorize applying a purge or mutating reconciliation.

skills/wiki-setup/references/search-diag.content:
# Diagnose search and index coverage

This procedure is read-only unless the user explicitly requests a particular
setup/repair action. Run quoted absolute installed helpers in the known vault.
Ordinary lookup uses [wiki-search](../../wiki-search/SKILL.md) without this preamble.

## Inspect the result and backend

1. Preserve the failing query, stderr status and JSON `channels`, `diagnostics`,
   `semanticGate` and freshness fields. Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" --health` for coverage. Use
   `--setup` only to display the exact remediation commands; display is not execution.
2. Distinguish reachable backend, pulled model and built/current index. Common
   causes are Ollama unavailable, embedding model missing or no index. Do not
   silently install/start services, pull models or run `index-embed.mjs` during diagnosis.
3. Report what succeeded and failed. A failed raw scan means not searched. A failed
   primary `wiki/` scan means incomplete coverage, even if other channels returned
   plausible results. Zero hits with failed coverage establishes no absence claim.

## Reading status and ranking

Keyword search scans `wiki/` and `moc/` Markdown: exact phrase, all query terms,
then partial matches. A chunk-level semantic index, built by `index-embed.mjs`
against Ollama, contributes Reciprocal Rank Fusion when backend and index exist.
Results report the actual matched `path:line` passage.

- `hybrid`: keyword and semantic channels contribute candidates. When one to three
  pages contain the whole query, or a query of at most five terms matches all terms
  within one paragraph on one to three pages, semantic candidates stop voting in
  final ordering. JSON `semanticGate: { reason, pages }` reports this; `null` means
  no gate. Tier stays hybrid because semantic still admits candidates.
- `lexical`: real keyword results, no semantic ranking. Say so in the report.
- `keyword request failed (wiki)`: the primary scope failed; other channel results
  do not restore that coverage. `channels.keyword.{wiki,moc,raw}` is `ok` or
  `failed`; semantic is `ok`, `failed`, `ollama-unavailable` or `index-unavailable`;
  identity is `ok` or `incomplete`. Inspect failed channels even under hybrid.
- `raw/ clippings NOT searched`: raw scan failed; no raw hits are not zero evidence.

Channel health does not establish relevance or factual truth. Return to the
retrieval workflow to open actual passages and check the user's claim.

## Index freshness and authorized remedies

Search validates candidate file versions against current files: modified semantic
hits are excluded until refreshed, removed hits dropped, and lexical/identity
hits may still have outdated embeddings. Candidate-limit notices bound what was
validated. Hash-keyed vectors do not make a stale manifest current. `--health`
reports changes since refresh; factual `reviewed` dates are a separate question.

`op-commit` attempts a semantic refresh after an ordinary mutation. Read its
notice: a committed change does not prove a successful/full index build. Hand
edits and changes pulled from another machine can make the index stale.

For an explicitly authorized rebuild, follow the exact supported setup output
and run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-embed.mjs"` only within that
scope, then rerun health and the original query. Apply the shared
[operation contract](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) if tracked
vault content changes; report local index/cache work separately. Never add a Git
remote or repair content merely to make diagnostics green. On backend failure,
report the remaining issue and use bounded lexical/filesystem retrieval.

# Validate exactly the task paths

Before committing, check exactly the pages the task wrote:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`,
with the vault set through [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md).
This procedure is read-only. A validation-only request opens no operation and makes
no edits, logs or catalog refreshes. For supplied paths, place a JSON ledger outside
the vault; an existing authoring operation may use its recorded ledger.

**The ledger** is the file `op-commit.mjs --paths-file` takes: a non-empty JSON array
of vault-relative paths with `/` separators (no drive prefix, backslash, empty segment,
`.` or `..`), for example `["wiki/authored/demo/guides/user.md","wiki/authored/demo/roadmap.md"]`.
Record each page you wrote with `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <path>...` (the log and
catalog scripts record theirs when given `--since`), then
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`
writes this file and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong (a path that was already
dirty before `op-begin`, a path that is not dirty now, a changed path nobody recorded). Writing
it by hand with your file tool still works. Keep it under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. A path with no file at that exact spelling is reported as `missing-file`: a page that
does not exist, or one whose letter case or Unicode form differs from the file on disk,
because a case-insensitive disk would otherwise drop that page's link checks without a word.

**The result.** The command writes nothing and reads the whole vault (ambiguity is
vault-wide), but reports only ledger pages; `health.mjs` stays the whole-vault check.
Exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects (fix and rerun), 2 means an unusable ledger, unknown
flag or missing vault. The text report is one `path:line rule message` line per defect,
sorted by path then line, then `validate-authored: N pages checked, M defects`, with
`, K skipped` appended only when K is above zero (checked plus skipped is the number of
distinct ledger paths). `--json` prints
`{"version":1,"checked":N,"skipped":K,"defects":[{"path","line","rule","message"}]}`
instead, which is exactly what `validateAuthored()` in `scripts/validate-authored.mjs` returns. An absent frontmatter key is reported at line 1; a blank key at its own line.

**Public pages.** A page written for a plugin's public repository must not name other projects or machines. `--terms-file <path>` (the owner's private list, kept outside every repository; the file `scripts/scan-private-terms.mjs` reads) adds a `private-term` defect for each ledger page whose text matches a term or a built-in machine pattern (a home-directory path, a GPU model, an invisible character), at its line, naming the rule number and never the text. `--terms-projects a,b` limits the check to pages whose `project:` (first segment) is listed, so a private project's own pages may name themselves. Without `--terms-file` the output is unchanged.

Under `wiki/authored/`:

- `missing-key`: `type`, `created`, `updated`, `status`, `ai-generated` and a
  `sources` line (`[]` is valid) must be present and not blank, so an unfilled
  template fails. A page in a project folder also needs `project` and `kind`, a
  decision `decision-status`, a backlog item `backlog-status`. `reviewed` is optional.
  A page missing one of those two statuses is judged by its declared `kind`, not its folder.
- `bad-value`: `type` is `authored`, `ai-generated` is `true` or `false`, and `kind`
  and the two statuses use the [project metadata vocabularies](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md#canonical-placement-for-original-project-documentation) (the message lists them). The page
  `status` is checked for presence only, so `status: wip` passes: check its value
  yourself against `stub`, `draft` and `maintained`.
- `kind-folder-mismatch`, `project-folder-mismatch`: `kind` agrees with the folder
  or file in the [project placement table](../../wiki-project/references/authoring.md#canonical-placement-for-original-project-documentation), `project` with the project folder (case ignored). The
  project is the folder path above the first kind folder (`guides`, `diagrams`,
  `reference`, `decisions`, `notes`, `backlog`) below the top folder, so
  `notes/<topic>/x.md` is a note and `project` must equal that folder path exactly.
  With no kind folder, `project` may be the top folder or the top folder plus one
  sub-project. `overview.md`, `architecture.md` and `roadmap.md` expect their own
  kind when they sit in a project folder. A page directly under `wiki/authored/` has
  no project or kind expectation. A wrong-kind page in `backlog/` gets only
  `kind-folder-mismatch`.

- `dependency-dangling`, `dependency-cross-project`, `dependency-self`, `dependency-cycle`,
  `dependency-malformed`, `dependency-misplaced`: a `depends-on` entry must be a
  wikilink to an existing backlog item of the same project (a note in `backlog/` is
  not an item). The message names the entry; a cycle names the whole loop and is
  reported on each ledger page in it. `dependency-misplaced` is `depends-on` on a page
  that is not a backlog item, where it is ignored. Only the item's own project backlog
  folder is read, so these checks add no second whole-vault scan.

On every wiki content page: `ambiguous-link`, `malformed-link` (a hard-wrapped link
is one), `unresolved-citation`, `malformed-frontmatter` (the page's metadata is not
read because of a stray carriage return or an unclosed fence), `missing-evidence`,
`cites-retired-page` (the cited page is marked `citation-status: retired`, so it is not support)
and `unresolved-link`, which is
stricter than health (it keeps such links as unscored forward links): a task must
not leave a dead link. Code spans and fences are not scanned. An absent file is
`missing-file`; raw, log, template, root catalog, non-Markdown and dot-prefixed paths
are skipped and counted.

Report exactly which paths were checked or skipped from the actual result. Generated
authored roadmaps are checked; they are not skipped just because they were generated.
A clean structural result is not a factual review. Repair requires authorization
from the owning project or maintainer workflow, followed by a fresh scoped check.

skills/wiki-setup/SKILL.md.content:
---
name: wiki-setup
description: Use when asked to initialize a wiki vault, check prerequisites, validate authored paths, report health, freshness, lint or ingest-backlog counts, diagnose search/index/app access failures, troubleshoot capture tools, or recover an explicitly authorized setup or operation failure. Reports and diagnosis are read-only; content repairs belong to wiki-maintainer.
---

# Set up, check and diagnose the wiki

Run the smallest procedure that answers the request. Reports, validation and
diagnosis are read-only: no operation, log, commit, index refresh or repair.
Initialization and recovery require the requested scope; a diagnostic result does
not authorize installing tools, rebuilding indexes, editing content or adding a remote.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the vault and absolute installed helpers from
   [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Read the actual applicable
   vault `AGENTS.md` before the first helper; do not infer its contents from a
   helper's output or skip it for validation-only work.
   Confirm the intended target and whether the request is report-only or authorizes
   a particular setup/recovery action. No app is needed for filesystem checks.
2. Select the matching procedure below. Run bounded checks and retain their actual
   exit codes, coverage and output. Distinguish no findings from failed coverage.
3. Explain the diagnosed state and its limits. If repair was not requested, stop
   with the report. Content defects route to
   [wiki-maintainer](../wiki-maintainer/SKILL.md); original documentation to
   [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).
4. Before an authorized mutation, read
   [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) and
   [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md); inspect existing operation
   state, preserve foreign edits and execute only the requested remedy. Verify
   its result using the relevant check and complete its owned transaction.

## Procedures and examples

- **Initialize:** read [initialization](references/initialization.md).
  Request: “Set up this new vault.” Action: preflight existing files and templates,
  open an operation, run `init.mjs` only when it cannot overwrite customized
  templates, inspect scaffold/health, log and close. Result: usable filesystem
  layout, existing content preserved, app registration and local-only status stated.
- **Validate changed pages:** read [scoped validation](references/validation.md).
  Request: “Validate these authored paths only.” Action:
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file "<ledger>" --json`.
  Result: checked/skipped counts and exact defects; no repairs or writes.
- **Health and backlog:** read [checks and metrics](references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog).
  Request: “How healthy is the wiki, and how many captures need ingestion?” Action:
  run `health.mjs --json` and `health.mjs --backlog`. Result: open integrity defects,
  coverage and the unsummarized-source count; no ingestion.
- **Freshness or lint:** read [freshness](references/checks.md#freshness-and-drift-coverage)
  or [content lint](references/checks.md#content-lint-report).
  Request: “Report stale pages and unsupported quotations.” Action: run read-only
  stale, drift coverage and scoped lint checks. Result: missing-review/stale pages,
  quote findings and coverage; dates, dispositions and content remain unchanged.
- **Search diagnosis:** read [search diagnostics](references/search-diagnostics.md).
  Request: “Why is search lexical only?” Action: run `search.mjs --health`, inspect
  backend/index state and report the cause. Result: an evidence-based diagnosis;
  displayed remediation commands are not executed without authorization.
- **Capture prerequisites:** read [capture prerequisites](references/capture-prerequisites.md).
  Request: “Check whether this machine can clip a presentation.” Action: inspect
  the PowerPoint converter prerequisites. Result: available/missing tools and
  supported fallback, with no invented capture or automatic installation.
- **App access:** read [app access](references/app-access.md).
  Request: “The native note-open action failed.” Action: inspect the guarded
  adapter's failure and canary result once. Result: the unavailable app action is
  reported honestly; independent filesystem work can continue.
- **Authorized recovery:** read [operation recovery](references/operation-recovery.md).
  Request: “Recover my failed scoped publication.” Action: reconcile the saved
  token, ledger and actual commit, retry only the unfinished step and verify the
  remote. Result: recovered publication or an exact blocker without duplicate edits.

## Best practices

Read-only means no cache-producing embedding evaluation either: use drift
`--coverage` for reports. A healthy graph is not factual verification; index
freshness is not a review date. Preserve failed checks and partial coverage in the
report. Check the current target before retrying an uncertain mutation. Never
remove another writer's token or Git lock to make a command succeed.

## Advanced references

The procedures above are conditional: load only the one the requested check needs.
Bounded embedding evaluation and verification cadence are in
[checks](references/checks.md#bounded-maintenance-evaluation); operation refusals,
Git settings and interrupted purge reconciliation are in
[recovery](references/operation-recovery.md). Follow the original action owner's
authorization boundaries even when setup supplies its diagnostic recipe.

## Done

A report states actual findings, checked scope, skipped/failed coverage and makes
no changes. Authorized setup/recovery verifies the requested effect and accounts
for its transaction/publication state; unresolved work has a precise next action.
